description: OpenCode custom-provider block + turn watchdog (Abilityai/lilu#257 step 6, the DGX-Ollama path). The provider half asserts the emitted `opencode.json` VERBATIM, because the failure mode is silent: a misshapen `provider.ollama` does not crash, it makes OpenCode fall back to its own default model on a turn the operator believes is running locally. `runtime: {type: opencode, model: "ollama/gemma4:12b"}` plus OPENCODE_OLLAMA_BASE_URL is sufficient on its own — the pinned model is always declared, so nobody maintains a parallel model list to use the model they already pinned; OPENCODE_OLLAMA_MODELS adds the extras. Base URL normalisation is idempotent (an operator who wrote /v1 does not get /v1/v1) and a non-http(s) value fails with a NAMED reason carrying the env var (quality bar 6), never a silent skip that degrades into OpenCode's own "unknown provider". Unset base URL emits no `provider` key at all, so the Anthropic/OpenRouter agent is untouched (graceful degradation); a foreign provider's model can never leak into the ollama model map; an operator-declared block wins on npm/options while its models are UNIONED, so a customised config can never be missing the model the turn was launched with; other providers survive the merge. The wiring is proven on disk through `_prepare_turn_config`, not just in the pure function. The watchdog half pins F6: the window before the first `step_start` is SILENT and was measured at 7.2s–59.3s for byte-identical configs on a real DGX (the variance is the provider's own model load), so the 300s default is ~5x the worst measured floor and is clamped to never exceed the turn timeout; a bad override falls back rather than disabling, because '0 means off' would let a typo remove the protection. A stall gets exactly ONE retry on a FRESH session (resuming the wedged session would reproduce the wedge) reusing the execution_id so the ledger shows one execution, not a phantom pair; a second stall is 504 and NEVER a success; a non-stall failure is not retried, since re-running a 500 would double every real error. The `step_start` event name is asserted against the real v1.18.32 stream — a rename would make the watchdog kill every healthy turn. Abilityai/lilu#272 adds the DERIVED default: with OPENCODE_OLLAMA_BASE_URL unset and the turn pinned to `ollama/…`, no block was emitted and OpenCode died in 1.6s with the opaque ref `err_411e3b55` — while the only value that works, the container's default gateway (host Ollama answers there; localhost is refused in 0ms), appeared in no config and no env and was unknowable without inspecting the host. The gateway is now parsed per turn from /proc/net/route, whose Gateway word is LITTLE-ENDIAN — the fixture pins 01001CAC -> 172.28.0.1, because read in string order it decodes to the plausible-looking, wrong 1.0.28.172. It is derived, never stored: the address belongs to the network the container is attached to, so a config key holding it would be wrong the first time the agent network is renumbered. The env var still wins (an operator pointing at a remote DGX is not redirected to their own host), a non-ollama turn with no env still emits NO provider key even when a gateway exists, and when neither path resolves the turn fails at the `-m` boundary — before any subprocess — with a reason naming OPENCODE_OLLAMA_BASE_URL rather than an `err_*` ref. The boundary guard refuses only the unrunnable: an operator-declared baseURL in the shared config satisfies it with no default route present. The `no default route` cases are asserted against fixture route files, never the host's own table, which would assert nothing inside any real container.
